transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-09-01
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~65 minutes
Attendees: Ava Chen, Priya Patel, Miguel Torres, Oliver Grant, Sofia Ramos, James Lee, Hannah Kim, Rajesh Patel
---
Summary: Quick product/engineering sync to go over Q3 roadmap items, launch readiness checklist for the upcoming Dedicated/Dedicated+Private rollout, incident items from last week's smoke test, and outstanding blockers. Agreed next steps and owners.
Topics: roadmap priorities, launch readiness checklist, incident review from staging smoke test, canary/fallback policies, QA/regressions, docs and runbook gaps.
---
[00:00] Ava: ok, hey everyone thanks for joining, we wanted to keep this tight 60-ish minutes, roadmap + launch readiness for the end-of-quarter push. Sofia, wanna kick off with product priorities?
[00:15] Sofia: yeah, quick recap. top priorities are 1) Dedicated capacity launch prep, 2) rollout for private control-plane (initial pilot), and 3) latency optimizations for long-tail requests. we still have the open TODOs on autoscaling policies and the canary plan, those are blockers for the commit.
[00:30] Priya: on the checklist i pulled the doc and added the release gating criteria — link in chat — but i think we need engineering sign-off on the capacity numbers and the fallback behavior when we exceed capacity, also need clarity on SLOs we ship with.
[00:45] Miguel: talking about SLOs, from the SE side we saw the staging smoke test last week hit spikes at ~1.8x expected qps which pushed latencies up. we need a clear plan to ensure prefix/KV caching isn't evicted too aggressively; otherwise p99 blows up.
[01:02] James: yeah, we observed cache churn when multiple models ran concurrent long sequences; some of the quantization variants have different mem profiles which made placement weird, i logged the host mapping in the spreadsheet.
[01:20] Oliver: can we be specific — what numbers do you need? is this about more reserved capacity or better routing? Miguel: a combination. we should tighten the routing policy so small latency-sensitive requests go to low-concurrency pools, and batchable background jobs go to high-throughput capacity.
[01:38] Priya: that aligns with the product ask: dedicated for customer X and routing policy A for low latency; we should document that in the rollout runbook. i'll own the runbook doc.
[01:50] Hannah: QA saw two flaky tests in the smoke run — one around tokenization differences between our python infra and the new compiled serving runtime, another around telemetry ingestion skews. both can cause false-positive regressions if not addressed.
[02:10] Rajesh: the telemetry skews are likely caused by delayed batching and the new kafka topic partitioning we tried. i'm going to revert that change in staging until we get the p99 behavior stable.
[02:28] Sofia: ok incident review action — Rajesh to revert the partitioning, Hannah to rerun regression matrix, Miguel to run an extended qps sweep. can we set targets? what are acceptable numbers for canary?
[02:45] Miguel: target p95 < 120ms, p99 < 450ms on latency-sensitive route with 99% of requests under 300ms during baseline load. during canary we tolerate 1.2x latency for transient warmups but not sustained.
[03:05] Ava: those look reasonable. we should capture them in the rollout gating criteria. Priya, add those thresholds into the checklist and we'll call that the launch SLO.
[03:20] Priya: will do. also need to call out encryption/KMS and audit log retention for the Private pilot — security flagged two items: key rotation policy and a missing audit export in the current private build. Sofia, can security help prioritize?
[03:35] Sofia: yes flagged to security, they're queued but not blocked — we need a small patch for audit exports which should be quick, key rotation is more policy than code.
[03:50] Oliver: re: canary/fallback — engineering proposes a staged rollout: 10% traffic for 48h, then 50% for 24h, then 100% if no regressions. automatic rollback if error rate >1% or latency regressions exceed the defined thresholds.
[04:10] Miguel: one nuance — for Dedicated we need manual override of autoscale for first week of the pilot, otherwise autoscale can oscillate with early traffic patterns.
[04:25] James: agreed, manual override is fine; i'll prepare the ops playbook and provide on-call contact list.
[04:40] Priya: docs and runbook owners then — Priya (runbook), James (ops playbook), Oliver (canary policy & thresholds), Miguel (benchmarks), Hannah (QA regression matrix). I'll add owners to the checklist.
[04:58] Ava: perfect. timeline — we want staging pass by 2026-09-07, canary start 2026-09-09, full launch 2026-09-15. Are those dates realistic?
[05:12] Oliver: tight but doable if the partitioning revert and latency sweeps finish this week. Miguel: i need until 09-06 to finish full QPS/latency matrix and submit results.
[05:28] Priya: i'll push the runbook tonight and ask for sign-offs in the morning.
[05:40] Hannah: QA will prioritize the regression runs and aim to provide a pass/fail matrix by 2026-09-05.
[05:52] Sofia: any other launch blockers? documentation completeness, customer communication templates, and the billing flow for Dedicated customers. billing team sync needed — who's owning that?
[06:06] Ava: Finance/Product Ops to own billing; i'll set up a follow-up with billing team and include Priya and James.
[06:20] Miguel: quick technical deep-dive note — long-tail sequences bring up the KV cache eviction problem; one mitigation is keeping a small hot-cache partition pinned for low-latency routes. that may increase memory footprint but helps p99. we should quantify tradeoffs.
[06:40] Rajesh: i'll work with infra to run a hot-cache experiment on a subset of nodes and report memory/latency numbers.
[06:55] Priya: also one small ask from legal/security — customer data retention defaults should be explicit in the pilot docs, and the Private pilot needs KMS integration notes. i'll add those to the runbook as TODOs.
[07:10] Ava: great. let's recap next steps quickly then wrap.
[07:20] Recap: Priya finalize rollout checklist (09-03), Miguel run sweeps & upload results (09-06), Oliver confirm canary/autoscale policy (09-04), Rajesh revert k-partitioning and run infra test (ASAP), Hannah produce regression matrix (09-05), James create ops playbook & oncall list (09-04), Ava schedule billing sync with Finance/Product Ops (09-02).
[07:50] Priya: noted. will send invites and the checklist doc link after the call.
[08:00] Miguel: i'll post benchmark CSV and raw logs to the shared drive, link in the checklist.
[08:10] Ava: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the doc and meet again if needed Friday to confirm staging pass.
[08:18] Sofia: thanks all, bye.
